tagline: Down a river that was given another river's name.
intro: From US 23 at Stratford, SR 315 runs about ten miles south to I-270 with the Olentangy beside it, east of the road the whole way, past the old stone houses the corridor is known for. It was the first road commissioned in Delaware County, in 1808.

The river's Delaware name meant sharp tool river, for the shale along its shores, and settlers called it the Whetstone. In 1833 the legislature set out to restore the old name and gave it "Olentangy" by mistake, a name that had belonged to what is now Big Darby Creek.

moments.title: Stratford
moments.text: Jonathan Crist built his limestone house in the 1840s onto his log tavern, and on this spot the town took the name Stratford on July 4, 1841.

moments.title: Bieber Mill
moments.text: Fully equipped it would have been the largest mill in Delaware County, but money ran short and only a sawmill ever ran, while the attached Knapp and Blinn grist mill kept working.

moments.title: Highbanks Metro Park
moments.text: Named for its shale bluffs high over the Olentangy, the park also keeps burial mounds and earthworks left by the Adena people.
